Create an automation: a project whose prompt a fresh agent runs on a schedule; --preview shows the next runs and creates nothing.

Usage: termag automation create <box>/<name> (--every <15m|30m|1h|6h|1d|1w> [--at <HH:MM>] | --at <HH:MM> [--weekdays] | --cron "<m h dom mon dow>") [--tz <zone>] [--from <github-url|template|box/project>]
       [--tier full|read] [--max-minutes <n>] [--no-pr] [--wake-box] [--space <name>]
       [--alert-prefix <text>] [--alert-regex <re>] [--alert-to dm|project|<channel-id>] [--no-health-alerts] [--webhook <https-url>]
       [--paused] [--preview] <prompt|->

--space <name> attaches the automation to a space you can write to (editor or owner). Its files
live in <space>:.termag/automations/<automation id>/, a folder fixed by its id: a rename never
moves it, and it is not space memory (agents in the space don't load it).

The folder holds README.md, memory/MEMORY.md, state.json and runs/<run>.md only while
automation-space-folder-enabled is on for the owner. With it off, only the notes file
(memory/MEMORY.md) is mirrored.

Alerts are sent by the orchestrator, so they arrive with your laptop off (automation-alerts-enabled).
--alert-prefix pings you when a finished run's STATUS summary starts with the text (BLOCKER:);
--alert-regex when it matches the pattern (`re` or `/re/i`; checked when saved).
--alert-to is where keyword and health alerts go: dm (your Slack DM, the default), project (the
project's Slack channel) or a channel id (C…, from the channel's details in Slack).
Health alerts name the cause of every pause (failed runs in a row, timeouts among them, the box
gone) and the first run skipped because the box was unavailable; --no-health-alerts turns them off.
--webhook POSTs run.done, run.failed and automation.paused as JSON to an https URL, signed with
X-Termag-Signature: t=<unix>,v1=<HMAC-SHA256 of "<t>.<body>">. The secret is printed once, when set.

Global flags:
  --json          Machine-readable output
  --yes           Skip confirmations
  --host <url>    Orchestrator to use (or TERMAG_URL). Default: the production orchestrator,
                  or this box's own orchestrator when run on a box
  -h, --help      Show help
  --version       Show the version

Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 failed, 2 usage error, 3 not found, 4 auth needed, 5 timeout.
